title: ARC: Fair Relative Advantage Comparison in Open-Ended Real-World Interaction
abstract: arXiv:2608.13622v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Open-ended real-world interaction admits multiple valid behaviors: an agent may answer directly, ask for clarification, provide progress updates, or confirm before acting. This flexibility breaks a core assumption behind group-based RL: rollouts compared within a group are no longer guaranteed to be behaviorally comparable. As a result, reward-model preferences over interaction style can distort relative advantages and steer optimization toward reward-preferred behaviors rather than context-appropriate ones. We formalize this as a \textit{reward fairness problem} and propose \textbf{ARC} (Advantage Regularization via Conditioning), a training recipe that restores fairer relative comparison through strategy-conditioned rollout grouping, together with hybrid rewards and entropy regularization. translated_title: ARC：开放世界真实交互中的公平相对优势比较
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13622v1 公告类型：新 摘要：开放世界的真实交互允许多种有效行为：智能体可以直接回答、请求澄清、提供进度更新或在行动前确认。这种灵活性打破了基于组强化学习的核心假设：组内比较的轨迹不再保证行为上具有可比性。因此，奖励模型对交互风格的偏好可能扭曲相对优势，并将优化导向奖励偏好的行为，而非上下文适当的行为。我们将此形式化为“奖励公平性问题”，并提出**ARC**（通过条件化的优势正则化），一种训练方案，通过策略条件化的轨迹分组、混合奖励和熵正则化来恢复更公平的相对比较。我们在我们提出的\inter中研究ARC，这是一种新颖的响应式、可引导且执行感知的用户-智能体交互范式，将用户可见部分与执行解耦。
tldr: 本文提出ARC训练方案，通过策略条件化轨迹分组和混合奖励，解决开放世界交互中奖励模型偏好导致的相对优势不公平问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes ARC, a training recipe using strategy-conditioned rollout grouping and hybrid rewards to address unfair relative advantages caused by reward-model preferences in open-world interaction.
